title: Xreal 1 Pro+ launches with brighter display and same price as predecessor
description: Xreal’s latest pair of AR glasses brings some big improvements on the display front while keeping the same $599 starting price. The key upgrade on the brand-new Xreal 1 Pro+ is its 1200 nits peak brightness, which is up from 700 nits on its predecessor. The new model now supports 60fps 2D to 3D conversion, up from 30fps on the Xreal 1 Pro, and this should directly translate to livelier spatial content. You get the same-sized 0.55-inch Sony Micro-OLED panels on the inside with 1920x1200 resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate. Xreal is advertising a new AI HDR feature, which should...

title: Samsung Galaxy A38's camera details surface
description: Yesterday, we learned that the Samsung Galaxy A58, expected to arrive next March or April, will feature the same camera setup as the Galaxy A57, at least in terms of resolution. The same source has now shared details about the Galaxy A38's cameras. The source claims that the Samsung Galaxy A38 will feature a 50MP primary camera, a 12MP ultrawide camera, a 5MP macro camera, and a 12MP selfie camera. That's the same as the Galaxy A37 launched earlier this year, at least in terms of resolution, because we don’t know whether Samsung will use larger or newer sensors. Samsung Galaxy...

title: RedMagic 12 Pro+ launches with RGB liquid cooling and a 185Hz screen
description: Right on schedule, the RedMagic 12 Pro+ was unveiled in China today, and it comes with what the company says is the industry's first 185Hz under-display 'true full-screen' display, not to mention the already teased RGB liquid-cooling system. It is of course powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, which is paired with the in-house RedCore R5 gaming chip. You can get up to 16GB of LPDDR5T RAM and 1TB of UFS 4.1 Pro storage, and an 8,400 mAh battery with support for 120W wired and 80W wireless charging, plus bypass charging and 22.5W reverse wired charging. The...

title: Here's when Apple will show off its touchscreen MacBooks and the OLED iPad mini
description: Last week, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that Apple is planning a second October launch following its smart home event, and now he has more details on what it will look like. According to Gurman, Apple is inviting some media to an all-day product launch experience on October 28 in Los Angeles. This will be for the touchscreen MacBooks, the OLED iPad mini, and the M6-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac. Gurman previously said the launch would happen on October 27, so it may very well be that Apple announces the new products that day and lets the press get hands-on with them a day...

title: Tipster says Galaxy S27 Ultra will have slightly thicker bezels than S26 Ultra
description: Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra is rumored to have nearly the same dimensions as its predecessor. However, according to a tipster, the new flagship could feature slightly thicker display bezels than the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Tipster Ice Universe claims that the Galaxy S27 Ultra will feature 1.28mm-thick display bezels, compared to 1.15mm on the current S26 Ultra. The tipster also claims that the rear camera bump on the upcoming flagship will be slightly thicker at 4.69mm, up from 4.5mm on the Galaxy S26 Ultra. However, the Galaxy S27 Ultra is rumored to feature a redesigned rear...

title: Amazon launches Bee Frontier AI wearable and Bee Eclipse phone attachment
description: Amazon today introduced two new Bee personal AI devices: the Bee Frontier wearable and the Bee Eclipse phone attachment. Both are meant to listen to your conversations and turn them into summaries, to-dos, reminders, and insights in the Bee app. You can wear the Frontier on a soft silicone wristband or clip it onto your clothes, and it comes in Lavender, Sage, and Onyx. It has dual microphones with noise filtering, IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, and USB-C charging. It's available now for $74.99. The Eclipse is about the size of a credit card, 4.6mm thick...

title: Boost Mobile teams up with Mike Tyson for its new ad campaign
description: Boost Mobile today announced a partnership with Mike Tyson, who will front its new US campaign called "What's Your Plan?". The name plays on the boxer's famous quote "Everybody has a plan until they get punched in the mouth", and in this case the punch is hidden fees, sudden rate hikes, and locked-in contracts from traditional prepaid carriers, as Boost puts it. Boost Mobile, which is owned by EchoStar, uses the campaign to highlight its no-contract approach and plans like the $25/month unlimited one, which it says is priced that way "forever". Bob Rupczynski, Group President of Boost...

title: YouTube is planning to add audiobooks to its Premium subscription, the WSJ reports
description: YouTube is in talks with publishers to add audiobooks to its service, reports the Wall Street Journal. This could be officially announced next year, but Google is yet to officially comment on the matter. Speaking of Google, the Google Play Store has offered audiobooks since 2018. However, you have to buy each book you want to listen to – there is no subscription. According to the Journal, YouTube will do the opposite – it will bundle audiobook listening with its ad-free Premium plan. Presumably, this will act as another selling point for the Premium plan compared to the cheaper Premium...

title: OpenAI sues Apple, claims an Apple employee stole proprietary info on an unreleased product
description: Back in July, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, claiming that two of its former employees stole proprietary IP from Apple and handed it over to OpenAI. Now the tables have turned – OpenAI claims that an unidentified employee left Apple, worked at OpenAI for six months and then returned to Apple with stolen details on OpenAI’s hardware projects. In its lawsuit, OpenAI alleges that this IP theft is related to the newly announced Apple HomeView hub. As you may have heard, earlier this year rumors started up that OpenAI is building a smart speaker that was developed in partnership with...

title: Verizon emphasizes its free safety, family, and AI perks
description: Verizon wants its customers to know they're getting more than just network access, and today it has listed all the perks that come with its plans at no extra cost. These cover safety, family, AI, and loyalty rewards, and some of them you may not have noticed so far. On the safety front, the free tier of Verizon Digital Secure protects connected devices from malicious websites and vulnerabilities. Verizon is currently offering one month of Verizon Digital Secure Premium for free too, so you can try out its extra safety tools. Verizon Family, with location sharing and Safe Walk, is included...

title: YouTube Music will now tell you if a song was made using AI
description: YouTube Music is rolling out new AI labels to help users identify songs created using AI. While artists using generative AI to make music is nothing new, listeners may not always know whether a track was created with AI. The “Made with AI” labels are rolling out on YouTube Music starting today and will arrive on the main YouTube app soon. Music featuring AI-generated compositions or vocals will display an AI label on the YouTube Music player page. Users can tap the label to learn more information. YouTube says it is using its own detection tools and teaming up with music industry...

title: Report: Samsung is expanding its display driver chip supplier pool
description: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 has been a pretty popular device, but Samsung has faced several issues in meeting consumer demand. On top of battling rising storage and RAM prices, Samsung has apparently hit a third bottleneck - display driver integrated circuits (DDIs). Display panel operation diagram (Samsung Display) These are specialized chips that serve as the interface between the phone’s CPU and display panel. They control sub-pixels and rendering using thin-film transistors and control color and brightness levels for each pixel on the phone’s screen. According to a recent ZDNet...

title: Here's when iPhone 18 production is rumored to start
description: Apple only launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in September, after plenty of reports said the vanilla iPhone 18 would be delayed until next spring. Today, a tipster on Weibo has shared a hint as to when production of the standard model will start. According to the tipster, the iPhone 18 is scheduled to enter production at the end of November. The tipster also says that, judging by the stock volume alone, Apple is preparing quite a lot of units. iPhone 17 Interestingly, a few days ago the same tipster claimed that expected iPhone 18 stock would be lowered, while Apple...

title: Samsung Galaxy A27, A37, A36, and A56 are receiving One UI 9 stable update
description: After rolling out the Android 17-based One UI 9 stable update for the Galaxy S23 series, Galaxy Z Fold5, and Galaxy Z Flip5, Samsung has now released stable One UI 9 for the Galaxy A27, Galaxy A37, Galaxy A36, and Galaxy A56. The stable One UI 9 update for the Galaxy A27 comes with firmware version A276KKSU3BZIF, while the Galaxy A37 update has firmware version A376NKSU3BZI6. Samsung Galaxy A27 The update for both smartphones is currently rolling out in South Korea, but it should expand to other regions soon. If you live in South Korea and haven't received the One UI 9 stable...

title: WhatsApp's new Guest Calling feature lets you invite anyone to a call
description: WhatsApp has announced a new Guest Calling feature that lets users invite anyone to join a call, including people who do not have a WhatsApp account. Guest calls also come without time limits and remain end-to-end encrypted. When a host invites someone to a call, the guest is placed in a waiting room and can join only after the host lets them in. Hosts can also remove guests at any time and guests cannot see other participants’ phone numbers, send them messages, or call them directly. However, guests can share their screens, send reactions, and raise their hands during calls. The...

title: More details about the iQOO Neo12's display revealed
description: iQOO is set to launch the Neo12 in China this month. It has already confirmed that the smartphone will feature a 2K 185Hz AMOLED display developed by Visionox and using p-TSF technology. Now, iQOO has revealed more details about the Neo12's display. iQOO said the Neo12's display will have a minimum brightness of 1 nit, while peak full-screen brightness will reach 2,200 nits. It also incorporates a 2K 185Hz high-performance driver chip and new Sky Mirror luminescent material. Furthermore, the Neo12 will come with 2K and 185 FPS super-resolution and super-frame processing, which iQOO...

title: Rumor claims the Oppo Reno17 series won't include a Pro model
description: The Oppo Reno17 series is rumored to launch in China next month. However, a new leak claims that the lineup will not include a Pro model, at least in India. Meanwhile, a hands-on image of the standard Reno17 has surfaced online. According to the leak, the Reno17 will retain most of its predecessor’s specifications and design. Oppo Reno17 leaked hands-on image The leak suggests that the Reno17 will feature the same Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 chipset and triple rear camera setup as the Reno16. The main upgrade could be a larger battery, with the upcoming phone tipped to pack a 7,000mAh or...

title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China, but without Siri AI
description: Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024 with iOS 18, but Apple struggled to make it available in two regions – the EU and China. Bloomberg reports that Cupertino will finally check the latter off the list with an upcoming update. iOS 27.3, which is expected in December, will enable Apple Intelligence for the Chinese market. While Apple uses Google’s Gemini in the West, it has struck a deal with Alibaba to use its Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang models. Qwen is a general AI model and will likely power most features. However, Siri AI will reportedly not be part of the iOS 27.3...

title: HMD is going to withdraw from "select markets", rumor claims
description: According to a new rumor from a usually reliable source of information about HMD, the company is currently planning on withdrawing from "select markets". It will also allegedly "scale down production for its global device portfolio". HMD is said to be shifting its "core focus" to "regional markets" as well as the enterprise/industrial sector. The same source goes on to imply that there may be no further HMD global product launches this year. Presumably, that means the company will only be releasing devices on a market-by-market basis in the coming months. Of course, this is nothing...

title: OnePlus Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro names confirmed by Google
description: The OnePlus Ace 7 had its specs leaked recently, and today, Google's official Supported Devices list has confirmed its name, while also revealing that it will have a sibling - the OnePlus Ace 7 Pro. According to Google's database, the Ace 7 has the model number PYF110, and the Ace 7 Pro has the model number PMS110. Both have run Geekbench 7 multiple times over the past few days, with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset at the helm.
